assigned.title: Playback-session candidate wire bounds match StreamCandidate bounds
assigned.acceptance: playbackSessionCandidateSchema uses THE SAME AUTHORITATIVE id and providerId limits as the StreamCandidate contract -- the exported MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS -- and NOT copied numeric literals. PL-0708 exported those constants for exactly this reason; a copied literal would recreate the defect one layer out, which is the defect this task exists to close. Required: an oversized resolved candidate CANNOT RE-EXPAND ON THE SESSION WIRE after passing through another producer seam, which is the actual risk -- the contract bound governs what a provider may produce, and a second unbounded restatement downstream means the bound stops at the seam; fixture and Wikidata legitimate identifiers remain accepted, because a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix; tests cover the EXACT MAXIMUM, MAXIMUM PLUS ONE, and the serialized response, since a bound tested only from above does not prove the boundary is where it is claimed to be; reason and error output does not echo the oversized value; and NO SECOND INDEPENDENT BOUND VOCABULARY IS INTRODUCED. Note while working: playbackSessionCandidateSchema also carries unbounded uri and mimeType. They are not named in the reviewer's acceptance and are not in scope by default -- if they warrant bounds, say so and let the reviewer rule rather than adding them quietly.

review.title: Production composition registers the catalog ingestion runtime
review.acceptance: A hosted deployment that is configured for a real catalog source actually gets one: something in the production composition root calls registerCatalogIngestionRuntime with a runtime built next to the Node pinned-fetch construction. PL-0305 made the application CAPABLE of hosting the real source and the reviewer accepted that as complete; what remains is that NOTHING CALLS THE REGISTRATION, so a hosted deployment still answers no_metadata_source_configured -- a true statement about the deployment rather than about the registry, and the exact gap this task owns. Required: the runtime is built from the existing pinned-fetch transport rather than a second fetch path; NO CREDENTIAL OR API KEY IS INTRODUCED, since the initial source needs none and an ambient key would be the hidden credentialed source PL-0305's review forbade; an unconfigured deployment must STILL refuse by name rather than silently acquiring a default; and a regression must drive the composition root and observe a configured resolution, because a registration nobody has watched fire is not known to work. OUT OF SCOPE: persistent scheduling and storage, which is PL-0309, and the rights register, which is not a coding task. NOTE BEFORE CLAIMING: the exact composition-root file may not exist yet; the declared surface names the likely homes and must be corrected before the claim rather than widened after, on the PL-0710 precedent.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 0 cached, 2642 passed 1 skipped (2617 before this wave). server-bootstrap.test.ts 16 passed; apps/web src/lib plus the entry point 162 passed. THE ENTRY POINT WAS PROVED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT CORRECTED THIS LEAD. My pre-claim surface correction moved instrumentation.ts to apps/web/ on the belief Next reads it from the app root; the implementer replayed Next 16.3.1's own findPagesDir and getFilesInDir and showed rootDir = path.join(pagesDir || appDir, '..') resolves to apps/web/src for a src/app project, so a file at the app root is NEVER LOADED -- and it REFUSED TO WRITE THE FILE AT MY DECLARED PATH rather than produce something Next never loads sitting where the wiring appears to be. The surface was corrected on that evidence and the probe now resolves instrumentationHookFilePath to /src/instrumentation.ts against the real tree, with a root-placed fixture resolving nothing as the control. VALUE-RED on the entry point: flipping the runtime guard from nodejs to node gives 2 failed 14 passed, 'runs the bootstrap in the Node runtime and the registry then resolves configured' and 'says so at startup when nothing is configured'. The ORIGINAL red for the composition root could only be module-resolution -- 'Cannot find module ./server-bootstrap', no tests collected -- because the gap this task owns is the ABSENCE OF A CALLER: there was no root to hand a wrong value, and the behaviour a value-red would assert already passed. Stated rather than smoothed. THE CREDENTIAL ASSERTION EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY: it is checked in two halves, every declared name against /KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|CRED|AUTH/i and the module's own source text against the declared set so a second undeclared read cannot hide, and it failed on the first green run because a comment named LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET -- 'expected [LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET, ...(8)] to deeply equal [...(7)]'. The pinned transport is asserted by REFERENCE IDENTITY, expect(runtime.provider.transport.fetchImpl).toBe(nodePinnedFetch), because a second fetch path that happened to work would satisfy any behavioural check. rightsRegister is noRightsBasisEstablished by reference, so a configured deployment publishes nothing and says per record why.

review.surfaceCorrectedTwiceBeforeCompletion: SECOND CORRECTION 2026-09-20, mid-implementation, AND IT REVERSES THE FIRST ONE. My pre-claim correction moved instrumentation.ts from apps/web/src/ to apps/web/ on the belief that Next reads it from the app root. THAT WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER PROVED IT rather than asserting it: Next 16.3.1 discovers the file in exactly one directory, non-recursively, at rootDir = path.join(pagesDir || appDir, '..'), so for an app with src/app and no pages/ the directory is apps/web/src and a file at apps/web/instrumentation.ts is NEVER LOADED. It replayed Next's own findPagesDir and getFilesInDir over this tree and over two throwaway fixtures differing only in the file's location, and the fixture with the file at the app root produced no instrumentationHookFilePath at all. It then REFUSED TO WRITE THE FILE AT THE DECLARED PATH, on the ground that a file Next never loads, sitting where the wiring appears to be, is worse than no file. That is the right call and the surface is corrected to match the evidence, which is exactly the bar the human commander set this round for touching a removed path. REMOVED as proved unnecessary: apps/web/instrumentation.ts (the wrong path); apps/web/next.config.ts (Next 16.3.1 needs no opt-in -- next/dist/server/config.js deprecates experimental.instrumentationHook with 'instrumentation.js is available by default', so the file earned no edit); docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (the operator note is a fact about this source and belongs in docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md, which already carries the licensing decision and the rights position, and the repo has no other deployment-runbook content for a new file to sit beside). ADDED: apps/web/package.json, because the app now imports @liberty/media-inspection for nodePinnedFetch and does not declare it -- the import resolves through the root workspace symlink so tsc and vitest are green and NO GATE CATCHES IT, which is precisely why the manifest must say what the app imports.

review.title: A configured catalog with nothing usable does not look empty
review.acceptance: The user-facing catalog path preserves the distinction the port now makes between no_records_usable and catalog_empty. apps/web/src/lib/catalog.ts maps an empty array to 'empty' and therefore COLLAPSES THE TWO, which is the one place PL-0305's four-state work stops short of the user. The two states have different causes and different remedies: catalog_empty means the source has nothing, while no_records_usable means records exist and every one of them was withheld -- almost always for want of an operator rights basis, which is an operator action rather than a user problem. Required: catalog.ts consumes describeCatalog through requireCatalogDescription rather than inferring state from an empty array; a source that does not implement describeCatalog still works and is not reported as a failure, because the method is optional on the port by design; the user-facing copy for the withheld case does NOT promise the content is coming, since nobody has committed to obtaining those rights; and the withheld reasons are not leaked verbatim to the user, because they name internal policy vocabulary. A regression must drive both states through the real loader and observe different answers.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 0 cached, 2642 passed 1 skipped. catalog.test.ts 33 passed (24 before); the six related suites 130 passed. TWO REDS OF DIFFERENT KINDS, REPORTED AS SUCH. Red 1 is a genuine value red: 'AssertionError: expected undefined to be catalog_empty' on a cause asserted against the unchanged loader. Red 2, the both-states regression, COULD NOT BE A VALUE RED THROUGH THE EMPTY PATH and the implementer said so plainly -- before the change the CatalogSource seam accepted only CatalogHomeResponse | null, which by construction carries no cause, so there was no input that would make the pre-change loader's two empty answers differ; the collapse was total, which IS the defect. What it produced instead was 'expected { status: error } to not deeply equal { status: error } -- Compared values have no visual difference'. NO WITHHELD VOCABULARY REACHES A RENDERER: readHomeCatalogFrom discards answer.withheld entirely and a test asserts JSON.stringify(result) contains none of rights_basis_not_declared, availability_not_stated, Q42 or Q7. TWO GUARDS BEYOND THE ASK: a source answering records_available whose records all have rights null is reported no_records_usable rather than catalog_empty, because works exist so 'the source has nothing' would be false; and catalog_empty from an answer with complete false is downgraded to cause_not_stated, because a prefix cannot support 'there is nothing there'. The implementer also DELETED 'No titles are currently available in your region', which asserted a cause nothing on the home path establishes, and flagged that as a judgement call rather than slipping it in. A source implementing no describeCatalog still loads and is not an error -- asserted, not assumed. NOT COVERED AND SAID SO: no test renders page.tsx, because apps/web has no React testing library and vitest runs environment node with no .test.tsx anywhere; the copy guarantee is enforced one level in, at the loader, and the does-not-promise property is a judgement published for the reviewer.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

recommended.title: Provider health contract
recommended.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

recommended.acceptance: GitHub becomes the shared state bridge for Claude Desktop and OpenAI review without manual file copying
